title: Legal English & Contracts
completion_message: ¡Excelente! El Inglés Legal (Legalese) es notoriamente complejo. Dominar términos como 'breach', 'liability' y 'arbitration' te protegerá en negociaciones y te permitirá interactuar con fluidez con los departamentos legales.

parts.visual:
Términos Legales Esenciales: 
- Breach of contract (Incumplimiento de contrato / Romper los términos acordados). 
Ej: Failing to deliver on time is a clear breach of contract. 
- Liability (Responsabilidad legal o financiera). 
Ej: The company denies any liability for the accident. 
- Arbitration (Arbitraje / Resolver una disputa fuera de los tribunales con un tercero). 
Ej: The contract states that any disputes will go to arbitration.
parts.audio: Essential Legal Terms. A 'Breach of contract' is the failure to observe a legal agreement. For example: Failing to deliver on time is a clear breach of contract. 'Liability' refers to being legally responsible for something, especially financially. For example: The company denies any liability for the accident. 'Arbitration' is the process of resolving a dispute outside the courts using an independent third party. For example: The contract states that any disputes will go to arbitration.

parts.visual:
Términos en Contratos: 
- Loophole (Vacío legal / Una ambigüedad en la ley o contrato que permite evadir una regla). 
Ej: They used a tax loophole to avoid paying millions. 
- Clause (Cláusula / Una sección específica de un contrato). 
Ej: Please read the termination clause carefully. 
- Binding (Vinculante / Que obliga legalmente). 
Ej: Once signed, this agreement is legally binding.
parts.audio: Contract Terms. A 'Loophole' is an ambiguity or inadequacy in the law or a set of rules. For example: They used a tax loophole to avoid paying millions. A 'Clause' is a particular and separate article, stipulation, or proviso in a treaty, bill, or contract. For example: Please read the termination clause carefully. 'Binding' means that an agreement involves an obligation that cannot be legally broken. For example: Once signed, this agreement is legally binding.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el término legal o de contrato correcto.

questions.question: If you do not pay by the deadline, you will be in ____ of contract. (Incumplimiento).
questions.explanation: Breach of contract = incumplimiento de contrato.

questions.question: The company accepted full ____ for the damages caused by the spill. (Responsabilidad legal/financiera).
questions.explanation: Liability = responsabilidad legal o civil (suele implicar pago).

questions.question: Instead of going to court, the two companies agreed to binding ____. (Arbitraje).
Their lawyers found a ____ in the tax code and saved them millions. (Vacío legal).
questions.explanation: Loophole = vacío legal, escapatoria en las reglas.

questions.question: A specific paragraph or section in a contract is called a ____. (Cláusula).
Once both parties sign it, the document becomes a legally ____ agreement. (Vinculante).
questions.explanation: Legally binding = legalmente vinculante / de cumplimiento obligatorio.

questions.question: When a court orders someone to stop doing something (e.g., selling a copied product), it issues an ____. (Orden judicial / Amparo).
questions.explanation: Injunction = orden judicial (generalmente para detener una acción).

questions.question: To start a legal case against someone is to ____ them. (Demandar).
Money paid to compensate someone for loss or injury is called ____. (Daños y perjuicios).
questions.explanation: Damages (siempre plural) = indemnización por daños y perjuicios.

questions.question: An agreement made outside of court to end a dispute, usually involving a payment, is a ____. (Acuerdo extrajudicial).
questions.explanation: Settlement = acuerdo (usualmente monetario) para no ir o para salir del tribunal.

questions.question: A person who brings a case against another in a court of law is the ____. (Demandante).
The person or company being sued or accused is the ____. (Demandado / Acusado).
Information kept hidden because of a Non-____ Agreement (NDA). (Acuerdo de confidencialidad).
questions.explanation: Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) = acuerdo de no divulgación/confidencialidad.

questions.question: If you fail to pay your mortgage, the bank might ____ on your property. (Ejecutar la hipoteca / Embargar).
An official document proving you own a piece of property (like a house) is a ____. (Título de propiedad).
questions.explanation: Deed = escritura o título de propiedad (también se usa 'title').

questions.question: Intellectual ____ includes patents, trademarks, and copyrights. (Propiedad intelectual).
A contract that says an employee cannot work for a competitor for a certain period is a non-____ clause. (Cláusula de no competencia).
questions.explanation: Non-compete clause = cláusula de no competencia.

questions.question: When a contract is officially cancelled and declared invalid, it is ____. (Nulo y sin efecto).
questions.explanation: Null and void = nulo y sin efecto.

questions.question: A legal process by which a person or business unable to pay debts is relieved of those obligations is ____. (Bancarrota).
The right to use someone else's property or land for a specific purpose is an ____. (Servidumbre de paso / Derecho de uso).
A ____ of contract. (Incumplimiento con B)
Legal ____. (Responsabilidad con L)
To go to ____. (Arbitraje con A)
A tax ____. (Vacío legal con L)
The termination ____. (Cláusula con C)
Legally ____. (Vinculante con B)
To ____ someone. (Demandar con S)
To pay ____. (Daños y perjuicios con D)
A non-____ agreement. (Confidencialidad con D)
Null and ____. (Sin efecto con V)
